items.title: Reduced holomorphic germ for a hypersurface
items.statement: For n≥1 and p∈ℂⁿ, a nonzero nonunit f∈O_{ℂⁿ,p} is reduced when no irreducible germ divides f twice. The zero and unit germs are excluded from hypersurface equations.
items.strategy: Translate to p=0; use the published UFD factorisation and local-unit criterion. This definition concerns the equation germ before identifying equations with the same geometric zero germ.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Square-free reduction of a holomorphic equation
items.statement: Every nonzero nonunit holomorphic germ f has a square-free reduction f_red=∏_{i=1}^r q_i, the product of its distinct irreducible factors. Its associate class depends only on f, and Z(f_red)=Z(f) as set germs.
items.strategy: Factor f=u∏q_i^{e_i} in the published UFD. Uniqueness gives the associate class, and the finite product has the same zero set as f on a common small representative neighbourhood.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Reduced preparation has nonzero discriminant
items.statement: If a reduced germ f is regular of order d in the last variable and f=uW is its monic Weierstrass preparation, then W is square-free in K[T], K=Frac(O_{n-1,0}), and Disc_T(W) is a nonzero holomorphic base germ. For n=1, K=ℂ.
items.strategy: Prepared factorisations preserve irreducible factors. Since O_{n-1,0} is a UFD, Gauss transfers square-freeness to K[T]; characteristic zero makes gcd(W,W′)=1, so the published discriminant/root criterion gives a nonzero base germ.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Finite local projection of a reduced hypersurface germ
items.statement: For a reduced nonzero nonunit f∈O_{ℂⁿ,p}, center coordinates at p and set f̃(z)=f(p+z). A generic complex-linear change in these centered coordinates and a small product neighbourhood give Z(f̃∘T)=Z(W) on V×D for a monic degree-d Weierstrass polynomial W. For the representative X_W=Z(W)∩(V×D), projection π:X_W→V is proper, surjective and has finite fibres; O_n/(W) is finite over O_{n−1}. Outside the nonzero discriminant D_W=0 it is a d-sheeted holomorphic covering. When n=1 the base is a point.
items.strategy: Translate p to the origin, choose a direction in which the centered germ has positive finite order, prepare, and shrink by the stable slice-zero count. Properness follows because the inverse image of compact K equals the zeros in K×closed D: continuity makes this set closed, and the slices have no boundary zeros. Division gives module finiteness; simple roots and the holomorphic IFT give local sheets away from the discriminant.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Discriminant and branch set of a fixed Weierstrass projection
items.statement: For a fixed monic reduced prepared equation W on V×D, put X_W=Z(W)∩(V×D) and define D_W(z′)=Disc_T(W) and branch set B_π={z′∈V:D_W(z′)=0} for the restricted projection π:X_W→V. The polynomial is unique for that fixed equation and projection (hence unchanged under unit multiplication of the original f), D_W is not identically zero, and B_π is exactly the base locus where the d distinct unramified sheets fail. The branch set depends on π and need not be the image of the singular locus.
items.strategy: Fix the product representative X_W=Z(W)∩(V×D) and its restricted projection π:X_W→V. Use uniqueness of Weierstrass preparation for the fixed projection, the coefficient discriminant and its repeated-root criterion, and the local-sheet part of finite projection. A repeated fibre root prevents d separate local sheets; a simple fibre gives them.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: A reduced prepared hypersurface stays reduced nearby
items.statement: For a reduced Weierstrass polynomial W defining a germ at p, after shrinking its product representative every local equation germ W_q at q∈Z(W) is reduced. This statement is for this principal hypersurface equation.
items.strategy: A nonreduced local germ W_q=g²h would force repeated roots on nearby slices. Choose the product and vertical disc entirely inside the neighborhood where this factorization holds, then use preparation and stable slice-zero count to place a zero of g over each nearby base point. At each such zero both W and ∂_T W vanish, so the discriminant vanishes on an open base set, contradicting its nonzero-germ identity theorem.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: The vanishing ideal of a reduced hypersurface germ is principal
items.statement: If f is a reduced nonzero nonunit holomorphic germ at p and X=(Z(f),p), then I_p(X)={h∈O_{ℂⁿ,p}:h vanishes on X}=(f). For arbitrary nonzero nonunit g with square-free reduction g_red, I_p(Z(g))=(g_red).
items.strategy: Prepare f=uW in generic coordinates. Divide a germ h vanishing on Z(W) by W. On the dense discriminant complement, the remainder polynomial of degree <d vanishes at all d distinct roots, so it is zero there; holomorphicity forces every remainder coefficient to vanish as a germ. The reverse inclusion is immediate. Apply the square-free lemma to nonreduced g.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Complex-analytic hypersurface germ and its reduced equation
items.statement: A nonempty proper hypersurface germ X at p∈ℂⁿ, n≥1, is the set germ Z(f) of a nonzero nonunit holomorphic germ f. Its reduced defining germ f_red is the square-free reduction; two reduced defining germs for the same X differ by a unit. The object is geometric and independent of the representative neighbourhood.
items.strategy: Existence comes from square-free reduction. The principal vanishing-ideal lemma identifies the ideals of any two reduced equations with I_p(X), so their generators are associates in the local domain. Agreement of representatives on a smaller neighbourhood gives the same germ.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Irreducible hypersurface germs and their components
items.statement: A hypersurface germ X at p is reducible when X=Y1∪Y2 for hypersurface subgerms Y1,Y2 properly contained in X, and irreducible otherwise; an irreducible component is a maximal irreducible hypersurface subgerm of X. Finite unions reduce to two-term unions via Z(g1)∪Z(g2)=Z(g1g2).
items.strategy: Unions and containments of set germs are read on a common neighbourhood of p; the product identity Z(g1)∪Z(g2)=Z(g1g2) groups a finite cover into two subgerms, so the two-term condition already captures finite reducibility.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Regular and singular points of an analytic hypersurface
items.statement: For a reduced hypersurface X near p, q∈X is regular exactly when the differential of a reduced local equation f_q is nonzero at q; otherwise q is singular. This is equivalent to X being a holomorphic hypersurface graph near q and is independent of the reduced equation.
items.strategy: If df_q≠0, the holomorphic IFT gives a graph. Conversely a smooth hypersurface has local coordinate equation w=0; the principal vanishing-ideal lemma makes f_q associate to w, so df_q≠0. Associates have the same nonvanishing differential on their zero set; the nearby-reduced lemma permits one fixed f on a small neighbourhood.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Irreducible holomorphic germs are prime
items.statement: Every irreducible germ q in the holomorphic UFD O_{ℂⁿ,0} is prime: if q divides a product ab, then q divides a or q divides b.
items.strategy: Assume q divides ab with neither factor divisible by q; the cofactor is a nonzero nonunit, and uniqueness of irreducible factorisation applied to ab=qc forces q to be associate to a factor of a or of b, a contradiction.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Finite unique irreducible components of a hypersurface germ
items.statement: Every reduced hypersurface germ X=Z(f) at p has a finite union X=⋃_{i=1}^r Z(q_i) of pairwise distinct irreducible hypersurface germs, where f is a unit times a product of pairwise nonassociate irreducible germs q_i. These components and their number are uniquely determined by X.
items.strategy: Use the local UFD for a finite factorisation and the principal vanishing-ideal lemma to identify I(Z(q_i))=(q_i). Primality proves each branch irreducible; reverse the containment argument using q_j vanishing on Z(q_i) to prove incomparability. Classify irreducible subgerms by factoring their reduced equations, and split any multiple-factor cover into one factor and the product of all remaining factors to prove both subgerms proper.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Krull dimension of the holomorphic germ ring
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For n≥0, dim O_{ℂⁿ,p}=n, with O_{ℂ⁰,p}=ℂ. For n≥1 its maximal ideal is generated by the n coordinate differences z_i-p_i.
items.strategy: Expand a holomorphic germ and group each nonconstant monomial by its first positive coordinate exponent to get f-f(p)=Σ(z_i-p_i)h_i with convergent h_i. The coordinate ideals form an n-step strict chain of primes since their successive quotients are smaller holomorphic germ domains. Under AC, apply the published Krull height theorem to the n-generated maximal ideal for the upper bound.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Local Krull dimension of a hypersurface germ
items.statement: For a nonempty hypersurface germ X at p in ℂⁿ, define dim_p X=dim(O_{ℂⁿ,p}/(f_red)), where f_red is any reduced local equation. The quotient and its dimension are independent of the equation and of the representative.
items.strategy: The vanishing ideal I_p(X) is intrinsically (f_red), so all reduced equations generate the same quotient ideal. Apply the published definition of Krull dimension to that quotient.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Reduced hypersurface germs have pure codimension one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every nonempty reduced hypersurface germ X⊂(ℂⁿ,p), n≥1, has dim_p X=n−1, and every irreducible component has this dimension and height-one defining prime. This asserts nothing about arbitrary analytic ideals.
items.strategy: Factor X into its irreducible q_i. For each q_i choose generic coordinates and preparation W_i. Division makes O_{n-1}→O_n/(q_i) injective and the quotient finite integral over O_{n-1}; under AC, integral-extension dimension preservation and the local dimension lemma give n−1. The published principal-ideal theorem/height-one corollary gives ht(q_i)=1 because q_i is a nonzero nonzerodivisor in a Noetherian domain.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Singular locus of a reduced analytic hypersurface
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a reduced hypersurface in a neighbourhood of p∈ℂⁿ, its singular set is locally the common zero set of f and ∂f/∂z_1,…,∂f/∂z_n for a reduced equation f. It is analytic and nowhere dense in X, and every nonempty germ of it has dimension at most n−2 (so it is empty when n=1).
items.strategy: The nearby-reduced and gradient criteria identify the equations. Every point off the fixed projection discriminant has ∂_T f≠0, hence Sing X lies over D_W=0. As O_n/(W) is free of finite rank over O_{n-1}, reducing modulo nonzero D_W stays finite integral with injective base map. Under AC, integral-extension dimension preservation and a prime-chain argument in the (n−1)-dimensional base domain give at most n−2. Root continuity and surjectivity of the finite projection show no component of X lies entirely over the discriminant, proving nowhere density.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Irreducible plane curve gives a connected punctured covering
items.statement: Let W(x,y) be an irreducible reduced Weierstrass polynomial of degree m defining a plane curve germ at 0. On a sufficiently small punctured x-disc, its zero set is a connected m-sheeted unramified covering, and each root tends to y=0 as x→0.
items.strategy: The one-variable discriminant has no zero off 0 after shrinking. The finite local projection supplies m sheets inside D, and the degree-m root count shows they are all roots over D*×C. Continuity on the closed vertical disc proves every root tends to 0, including limits that could initially lie on ∂D. If the cover had a proper component, its monic root product would have bounded symmetric coefficients; removability and the root limit extend them with zero values at 0, giving a positive-degree Weierstrass factorization and contradicting irreducibility.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Convergent Puiseux parametrisation of an irreducible plane branch
items.statement: Every irreducible plane curve germ through 0 admits, after complex-linear ambient coordinates, a primitive injective holomorphic parametrisation γ(t)=(t^m,h(t)), m≥1, h(t)=Σ_{k>m}a_k t^k convergent near 0, whose image is exactly the germ. In fixed coordinates with first component t^m, such primitive parametrisations differ only by t↦ζt with ζ^m=1. Thus the Puiseux series y=h(x^{1/m}) is convergent; no formal-only claim is used.
items.strategy: Use the local irreducible-decomposition and vanishing-ideal route to establish algebraic irreducibility, then use the connected m-sheeted punctured-disc cover. Its slit continuation gives an m-cycle. Pull back along x=t^m; IFT root graphs glue across slit fibres, including boundary rays, and the corrected radius δ=ε^(1/m) stays inside the base disc. Bounded roots and removability extend h through 0; separated fibres give injectivity and exhaust the image.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Total quotient ring and normalisation of a reduced plane curve germ
items.statement: For a reduced plane curve germ X, set A=O_{ℂ²,p}/I_p(X) and S={a∈A:a is a nonzerodivisor}. Define Q(A)=S^{-1}A and the normalisation of A as the elements of Q(A) integral over A. For a single branch this is integral closure in its fraction field.
items.strategy: The vanishing ideal makes A independent of the reduced equation. Multiplicativity of S follows from composition of injective multiplication maps; localization and integrality are the declared published interfaces. The product description for several branches is proved in the next lemma.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Total fractions split over the branches of a reduced hypersurface
items.statement: If f=q_1⋯q_r is a reduced product of pairwise nonassociate irreducible germs in the holomorphic UFD O_n and A=O_n/(f), then Q(A)≅∏_{i=1}^r Frac(O_n/(q_i)). For r=1 this is the ordinary fraction field.
items.strategy: The map A→∏O_n/(q_i) is injective because the intersection of the principal prime ideals (q_i) is their product. Put s_i=∏_{j≠i}q_j and s=Σ_i s_i; s avoids every (q_i), hence is a nonzerodivisor in A. The fractions s_i/s supply the coordinate idempotents in Q(A). For any nonzero denominator in component i, alter a lift by λq_i; only finitely many λ∈ℂ make it divisible by one of the other q_j, so choose another λ and obtain a nonzerodivisor denominator. This realizes every component fraction and proves surjectivity without invoking an unplanned normality theorem.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: Puiseux discs normalise a reduced plane curve germ
items.statement: For a reduced plane curve germ X with irreducible branches X_i, the Puiseux maps γ_i(t)=(t^{m_i},h_i(t)) induce a finite birational integral embedding A=O_{ℂ²,p}/I_p(X) into ∏_iℂ{t_i}; the latter is exactly the integral closure of A in Q(A). The discs separate the finitely many branches, and each map is a biholomorphism away from its singular point after shrinking.
items.strategy: For each branch, the substitution A_i→ℂ{t} is injective by the principal vanishing-ideal lemma. Decompose convergent series by exponents modulo m to make ℂ{t} finite over ℂ{t^m}⊂A_i. Gauss transfers irreducibility of the monic W to Frac ℂ{x}[y], so [Frac A_i:Frac ℂ{x}]=m; compare [Frac ℂ{t}:Frac ℂ{x}]=m to get birationality. A negative-order Laurent germ cannot satisfy a monic equation with holomorphic coefficients, so ℂ{t} is integrally closed. Apply the preceding total-fraction product lemma; the finite product of the finite branch normalizations is finite over A and thus integral, while componentwise normality gives the reverse containment of the integral closure. Injective Puiseux maps and the unramified punctured covering give geometric branch separation.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

title: Analytic Hypersurfaces and Local Parametrisation: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A regular hyperplane has a one-sheeted projection
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For X={z_n=0}⊂ℂⁿ, the reduced equation z_n has nonzero differential everywhere. The global coordinate projection X→ℂⁿ⁻¹ is the identity; on the product representative X_W=Z(z_n)∩(V×D), the finite local projection has discriminant 1 and empty branch set. The quotient dimension is dim₀X=n−1.
items.strategy: Distinguish the two projection claims: the global coordinate projection X→ℂⁿ⁻¹ is the identity, while the finite theorem applies to X_W=Z(W)∩(V×D) with its restricted local projection. For W=z_n the discriminant is 1 and the local branch set is empty. The quotient by (z_n) is O_{n-1}, giving the dimension under the declared AC dimension interface only if that numerical dimension is invoked.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: An ordinary node has two smooth branches
items.statement: Near 0 the reduced curve y²=x²(1+x) is the union of the two smooth branches y=±x√(1+x); the origin is singular and each branch has a convergent parametrisation with first coordinate t.
items.strategy: Apply the holomorphic IFT to s²=1+x at (0,1) to construct the unit square root. Factor f=(y−x s(x))(y+x s(x)); the factors are distinct and smooth, while ∇f(0)=0. Parametrise each graph by x=t.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: The cusp y²=x³ has Puiseux parameter (t²,t³)
items.statement: The plane curve germ y²=x³ is irreducible and singular at 0; t↦(t²,t³) is its injective convergent Puiseux parametrisation.
items.strategy: Factor the monic quadratic correctly: in a nontrivial factorization the leading coefficients are units, so neither factor can be constant; normalize the linear factors and compare coefficients to get a square root of x³, impossible by odd order. Substitution, gradient and fibre calculations verify the parametrisation and minimal exponent.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: The coordinate axes form a reduced crossing
items.statement: The reduced plane curve xy=0 consists of two distinct smooth branches x=0 and y=0. Its only singular point near 0 is their crossing at 0, and no single injective branch parametrisation covers both components.
items.strategy: Factor the reduced equation x·y, apply the local decomposition, and compute ∇(xy)=(y,x). If a holomorphic map from one connected disc has image in the union, its coordinate functions have product zero; the one-variable instance of the holomorphic identity theorem forces one coordinate to vanish identically. Thus one branch parametrisation cannot cover both components.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: A nonreduced equation can hide a smooth hypersurface
items.statement: The equations x=0 and x²=0 define the same smooth hypersurface germ in ℂ². The raw differential of x² vanishes on it, whereas the differential of its reduced equation x is nonzero.
items.strategy: Square-free reduction of x² is x up to a unit; compare zero sets and compute the two gradients. This verifies why the regularity criterion specifies a reduced equation.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: A branched projection of a smooth hypersurface
items.statement: The reduced curve y²=x is smooth at (0,0), but its projection (x,y)↦x has discriminant 4x and branch set {x=0}. Thus branch points of a selected projection do not equal singular points of the hypersurface.
items.strategy: Use the fixed x-projection on |x|<epsilon, |y|<r with epsilon<r^2. Both roots stay inside; compact preimages and implicit holomorphic sheets prove properness and the two-sheeted cover away from zero. The gradient (-1,2y) proves local reducedness and regularity, while discriminant 4x gives branch set {0}.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: The plane branch y²=x⁵ has Puiseux parameter (t²,t⁵)
items.statement: The plane curve germ y²=x⁵ is irreducible and singular at 0, with injective convergent parametrisation t↦(t²,t⁵). Its Puiseux exponent 5/2 differs from the cusp y²=x³.
items.strategy: Factor the monic quadratic correctly: in a nontrivial factorization the leading coefficients are units, so neither factor can be constant; normalize the linear factors and compare coefficients to get a square root of x⁵, impossible by odd order. Substitution, gradient and fibre calculations verify the parametrisation and minimal exponent.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6

items.title: The single-equation proof does not cover arbitrary analytic sets
items.statement: The analytic germ {0}⊂ℂ² is cut out by (x,y) and cannot be the zero germ of one nonzero holomorphic function. Its arbitrary-ideal singularity and parametrisation questions need arguments beyond this hypersurface proof, including coherence in the standard general theory.
items.strategy: The published zero-set theorem excludes isolated zeros of a nonzero holomorphic function in ℂ². The two coordinate equations cut out {0}; hence the single-equation Weierstrass and gradient proof cannot be applied to every analytic ideal.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 6 §§6.1–6.7
Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §§2, 4 and 6
